soloProfile.summary: Solo is for psychological sci-fi, jaw-drop reveals, workplace comedy, dark satire, and anything Helen would bounce off: superhero, sci-fi/fantasy, crude humour, slow cerebral drama.
loves: Mystery boxes that resolve (Severance, Dark, Silo)
Dry, sharp dark comedy (Barry, The Great)
avoids: Open-ended mystery boxes that never pay off (Westworld)
Slow and intense with no payoff (Mindhunter)
Shows that only get good after two or more seasons

togetherProfile.summary: Together works on momentum: spy and crime thrillers, prestige true stories, period drama and warm, relatable comedy. Dark is fine when it is purposeful and moves; slow, bleak or silly is where Helen drops out.
loves: Spy and crime thrillers (Slow Horses, Bodyguard)
Prestige true stories, especially WWII with hope
Period drama (The Crown, The Gilded Age)
Dry, grounded wit over zany humour
avoids: Bleak shows with no purpose (Happy Valley)

solo.title: The Expanse
solo.reason: Top of your solo start list. The protomolecule arc is a slow-release mystery box with real jaw-drop payoffs, six complete seasons and an ending that lands — your Foundation and Silo lane exactly. On Prime Video.

solo.title: The Paper
solo.reason: In progress and rated 4★ — you said it found its footing after a few episodes and might go higher. Easy-watch workplace comedy in your Office-lineage lane; finish what's aired. On Binge.

solo.title: Abbott Elementary
solo.reason: In progress and rated 4★. Low-commitment half-hours for whenever you want a comfort comedy between heavier shows. On Disney+.

solo.title: VisionQuest
solo.reason: You're two episodes in. The close of the WandaVision trilogy, with critics calling it humane and hopeful — keep going while it's fresh. On Disney+.

solo.title: Mr Inbetween
solo.reason: In progress. Australian hitman dramedy with bone-dry wit and short episodes — Barry 4★ is the comp. Three seasons, complete. On Binge.

solo.title: 12 Monkeys
solo.reason: Time-loop thriller that becomes a payoff machine, building to a finale that famously sticks the landing, with twisty episode-end hooks from the start. Four seasons, complete. On Prime Video.

solo.title: Devs
solo.reason: Alex Garland's determinism thriller — eight episodes, fully resolved, in the Severance and Dark lane. Slow and cerebral, so a solo watch. On Disney+.

solo.title: Justified
solo.reason: Dry, deadpan Elmore Leonard crime with a real serialised spine in Raylan versus Boyd. Six seasons that end well. On Disney+ and Binge.

solo.title: The Night Of
solo.reason: Eight-episode murder case that becomes a takedown of the justice system. Contained, complete and gripping. On Prime Video.

solo.title: Six Feet Under
solo.reason: A prestige classic with a famous final episode. Heavy subject matter with dark humour as the buffer; expect a 4★ watch, not a binge. On Prime Video.

solo.title: Rake
solo.reason: Australian legal comedy-drama with Richard Roxburgh as a gloriously self-destructive barrister. Hacks 4★ is the comp, but this is episodic enough to judge in three episodes. On Prime Video.

solo.title: Marvel's Jessica Jones
solo.reason: Rated 4★ and paused on purpose — your note says you want to catch up on the other Marvel Netflix shows first. Pick it back up once those are done. On Disney+.

together.title: Band of Brothers
together.reason: The strongest together start in your library: Chernobyl's structural twin — true-story WWII prestige, ten episodes, complete. Heavy, but purposeful and hopeful, the shape that just landed 4.5★ with We Were the Lucky Ones. On Prime Video.

together.title: The Rookie
together.reason: In progress and rated 4.5★ — your top-rated together show still airing. Keep up with the current season. On Disney+.

together.title: Broadchurch
together.reason: In progress and rated 4★ with binge 5. Finish the remaining series — it's the together crime sweet spot. On Prime Video and Binge.

together.title: Line of Duty
together.reason: From Bodyguard's creator (4★ together) — propulsive anti-corruption thriller built on legendary interrogation scenes. Each season is a self-contained case, so you can stop cleanly. On Binge.

together.title: Unforgotten
together.reason: Cold-case British crime with Nicola Walker; each series is a self-contained case. The Broadchurch lane, gentler. On Binge.

together.title: Ludwig
together.reason: David Mitchell as a grumpy puzzle-setter impersonating his detective twin — cosy case-of-the-week with the dry-wit lead Helen loves. On Binge.

together.title: High Potential
together.reason: Procedural with a serialised spine — a single mum with an exceptional mind, plus the mystery of her missing husband. Easy weeknight watch. On Disney+.

together.title: Friday Night Lights
together.reason: Ignore the football: it's a grounded marriage-and-family drama built around Coach and Tami Taylor. Five complete seasons. On Prime Video and Binge.

together.title: Say Nothing
together.reason: Nine-episode true story of the Troubles built on a disappearance and its cover-up. Grim but purposeful, with a real mystery spine. On Disney+.

together.title: Wolf Hall
together.reason: Mark Rylance as Thomas Cromwell — The Crown's together lane, complete across two runs. Slower and more austere, so one for a focused evening. On Binge and Prime Video.
